column1: # Reset-polarity census.  Produced by formal/lean/scripts/reset_polarity_census.py,
# which reads the two places a certificate records a reset polarity and reports
# whether, and how, they can be compared.  Raw dumps (UNTRACKED, /generated/ is
# gitignored):
#   generated/master_port/fp/proto_modes/reset_polarity_imported.{log,json}
#   generated/master_port/fp/proto_modes/reset_polarity_master.{log,json}
# WHY THIS EXISTS.  DirectCheck.lean declines to cross-check reset polarity and
# gives this reason (lines 107-111):
#   "an async flop's `resetPin` slot and its `resetInput` ordinal legitimately
#    differ in POLARITY -- the census shows 9,262 async sources whose `activeLow`
#    is the opposite of their `FlopDesc.resetActiveLow`, because the pin slot
#    reads an already-inverted node while the ordinal reads the raw port."
# That justification is CONDITIONAL on the pin slot being a NODE.  The 9,262
# figure has no retained artifact anywhere in this tree (the comment arrived
# with the D2 port, 106531b2e, and the census itself did not), so this file is
# the retained one.  The classes below make the condition observable:
#   node-mediated        FlopDesc.resetPin resolves to a NODE slot.  The two
#                        sides read different signals; opposite polarities are
#                        expected and nothing is comparable.  DirectCheck's case.
#   raw-port:agree       resetPin resolves to the SAME .input ordinal the
#                        flopQAsync source names, and the polarities match.
#   raw-port:OPPOSITE    same single .input ordinal, opposite polarities.  No
#                        value of that port leaves both paths out of reset.
#                        DirectCheck's reason does NOT cover this case.
#   no-flop-reset        FlopDesc carries no reset pin; nothing to compare.
# SEMANTICS BEING COMPARED (both sides use the same convention):
#   read side    Runtime.lean:83   asserted = if al then !(bv_nonzero r) else bv_nonzero r
#   commit side  DesignSemantics.lean:67,113   asserted = xor resetActiveLow (bv_nonzero (rho r).asBV)
corpus
imported pre-D2 CVA6 (livehd-d4-incremental/temp/cva6_30_auth + cva6_30_auth2)
column10: EVERY reset-bearing flop points resetPin at a RAW .input and carries activeLow=0, while the same port's flopQAsync source carries al=1.  2705/2705 flop rows are 0 and 2673/2673 source rows are 1 in cva6_30_auth alone -- no counterexample on either side.  Not the node-mediated case: node-mediated count is ZERO.

column1: master-emitted (generated/master_port/**: pilots, D3/D4 corpora, parity sets)
column10: ZERO raw-port oppositions.  Master points resetPin at the already-inverted NODE, which is exactly the shape DirectCheck describes, and writes the SAME polarity bit on both sides (certificate_ir.cpp:74 and :345 both assign f.active_low; emit_dcert.cpp:169 and :231 both emit reset_active_low), so the two fields are structurally incapable of disagreeing.  The 2 raw-port:agree rows are the tiny_async parity fixture.

column1: hand-written FP fixtures (generated/master_port/fp/fixtures/dcert)
column10: No opposition.  seq.dcert has a SYNCHRONOUS reset (flop reset slot is a raw .input with no matching flopQAsync source: class no-async-source); wide.dcert drives its one reset-bearing flop from a const slot (class slot-is-const).
